subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw core support opt-in model-mediated SOUL.md auto-evolution, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses core agent runtime, config, session-state, CLI, and security boundaries, and repository policy treats new config and instruction-file persistence as maintainer decisions before implementation.

options.title: Accept default-off core SOUL persistence
options.body: Continue reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95793, but require the security and delivery fixes before merge.

options.title: Move preference capture to memory/plugin APIs
options.body: Close or redirect the linked PR and define the missing plugin/API seam needed for safe external implementation.

options.title: Defer automatic instruction-file writes
options.body: Keep SOUL.md manual and document that durable user preferences should live in the existing memory flow for now.

recommendation.title: Accept default-off core SOUL persistence
recommendation.body: Continue reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95793, but require the security and delivery fixes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved blocker is a core product/security boundary rather than a narrow code repair, and this owner has the strongest available SOUL docs and vision-routing signal.
